add_param.edit: add a trailing `int aerotrace_bench` parameter to the definition and every prototype of that function (same-named functions in other files are left alone); calls unchanged
add_param.why: every direct caller stops compiling; drawn from functions with 10 to 150 direct calls (wide fan-out)

remove_fn.edit: delete the definition; any prototype stays
remove_fn.why: callers fail to compile, or, when a prototype stays in a header, only at link

int_to_void.edit: change the return type from int to void in the definition and every prototype; `return X;` becomes `(void)(X); return;`
int_to_void.why: only callers that use the value break; callers that ignore it still build

ptr_param.edit: add a trailing `int aerotrace_bench` parameter to the definition and every prototype of a function that is called directly and also stored as a pointer; calls and tables unchanged
ptr_param.why: direct calls break, and so does the place it is put in a table or assigned to a pointer

ptr_remove.edit: delete the definition of a function that is reached only through a pointer; any prototype stays
ptr_remove.why: nothing calls it by name; only the table or assignment that names it breaks

field_rename.edit: rename the struct field to `<name>_renamed` in the struct only
field_rename.why: every reader and writer breaks; same-named fields of other structs must not be counted

field_type.edit: change the type of an integer struct field to `void *`
field_type.why: arithmetic and integer uses break; some uses still build and may behave differently

global_rename.edit: rename the definition of a file-scope variable to `<name>_renamed`; any `extern` stays
global_rename.why: every use breaks (at compile time, or at link when an `extern` stays)

macro_arity.edit: add a trailing parameter `aerotrace_bench` to every `#define` of the function-like macro
macro_arity.why: every use breaks; macros are a common gap for tools that read the code after the preprocessor

behaviour.edit: make the function return the zero value of its type (0, NULL or false) as its first statement
behaviour.why: nothing fails to build; callers that use the value may behave differently (truth checked by hand)
